status: unexecuted fixture and source-derived observation contract; no browser or candidate observation

harness_contract.ready: Wait for c04-ready or inspect c04BootstrapError; a bootstrap failure fails the reference attempt.
harness_contract.input: Initial query parameters: animations=enabled|noop, preserve=true|false, contentTabIndex=0|unset, selected=0|1. Bounded runtime setters accept preserve boolean and contentTabIndex null or 0; selected accepts 0 or 1. Call setters independently and observe resulting state.
harness_contract.observation: Capture full snapshots at initial settling, immediately after each action, first animation frame, and completion: event sequence with timestamp/action marker, panel and content wrapper styles and rects, child and focusable descendant styles and rects, local animation records, DOM and focus, and lifecycle. getAnimations subtree support is feature-detected; unavailable or throwing yields inconclusive, not motion completion. Capture CDP AX separately.
harness_contract.user_actions: Use actual browser pointer and keyboard actions on role=tab elements, not synthetic events or internal members. Call markExternalAction immediately before each such action to mark the event stream; action IDs record observation context, not causal proof. Focus/select and bounded state setters use NgZone.run.
harness_contract.completion: For initial settling, waitFor with requireAnimationDone=false requires selected DOM agreement, two stable frames and no pending/running local animations. Before each transition save the event-array length and call waitFor with afterEvent and requireAnimationDone=true; it also requires selected DOM agreement, two stable frames and no pending/running local animations. Missing event or deadline is inconclusive/failure, never a passing fixed sleep. Unsupported animation inspection is explicitly inconclusive. A void animationDone after the cursor cannot prove which cancelled or reversed cycle produced it; retain all timestamps and action markers for external analysis.
harness_contract.identity: Compare panel name and instance number across snapshots with lifecycle create/destroy events. The child is a lazy consumer ng-template so its lifecycle is observable without modifying the library.
harness_contract.isolation: Reference and candidate run in independent pages and injectors with the same browser binary, viewport, DPR, fonts, action sequence and appropriate styles. Never create reference expectations from candidate output.

source_grounded_expectations: The 16 tab-group template gives each tab role=tab, aria-controls, aria-selected and each panel role=tabpanel, id and aria-labelledby; compare actual associations, not generated identifier spelling.

Only the selected panel receives the configured contentTabIndex when non-null; no panel gets the attribute when it is null. The original group panel template has no aria-hidden binding; record the actual attribute without imposing it as an accessibility rule.

The original declares selectedTabChange, selectedIndexChange and animationDone outputs. Record emitted values and order; do not assume every operation emits any particular sequence without runtime evidence.

preserveContent retains previously attached tab content; with preservation disabled the original may detach it after its leaving transition. Observe identity and lifecycle after actual completion, rather than assuming exact timing or focus relocation.

limitations: No build, JIT bootstrap, browser, accessibility or runtime observation has been performed.
Compiler 16 package integrity and isolated reference environment remain to be established. Angular 16 partial-compiled JIT compatibility is unproved.

waitFor relies on requestAnimationFrame, local Web Animations inspection and public animationDone; missing events or unsupported inspection are inconclusive. The void event cannot identify a cancelled or reversed transition; inspect the complete recorded sequence externally. Feature detection cannot independently establish that a browser correctly implements the subtree option.

Stable selected DOM alone does not establish that an animation is complete. CSS must be supplied equally by the later independent harness; this fixture does not fabricate the original component styles.
No screen-reader behavior or owner qualification is claimed.
CSS rects and computed styles are observations, not alone proof of accessibility-tree exposure. Non-local animations or CSS behavior outside the tab group are outside local animation inspection.
